 Thousands of pet medications recalled nationwide due to potential potency issues
 Recalled items include liquids, powders, sprays, eye drops, and injections
 10 News Digital Team
 Published:  October 26, 2026 at 6:25 AM Tags:  Recall , animal medication safety , veterinary pharmacy alert , pet medication potency (Manuel Balce Ceneta, Copyright 2020 The Associated Press. All rights reserved.) If you have pets, a recall has been issued that you will want to keep on your radar. Nearly 4,000 medications used to treat pets and other animals are being recalled nationwide over concerns they may be too strong or too weak. 
 New Jersey-based Wedgewood Pharmacy announced the recall after testing found inconsistencies in the strength of some medications. 
 Recommended Videos
 The affected products were shipped to veterinary practices, pharmacies, and other customers across the country between Feb. 18 and Oct. 6.
 The recalled products include liquids, powders, sprays, eye drops, and injections used to treat dogs, cats, horses, fish and other animals.
 The health risks associated with low potency can include ineffective treatment, while the health risks involved with high potency can include toxicity or even overdose. 
 So far, Wedgewood has received 98 complaints, seven of which the company described as serious. Customers are urged to contact their veterinarians if they have medical concerns.
 For a full list of the products involved in this recall, click here.
